test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which non-constitutional body investigates corruption complaints against public servants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lokpal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lokpal** is an independent statutory body in India that investigates complaints of corruption against public servants, including the Prime Minister, Union Ministers, Members of Parliament, and other public officials.
 
• The **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**, provides for the establishment of Lokpal at the central level and Lokayuktas at the state level to combat corruption in public administration.
 
• The Lokpal consists of a **Chairperson** and a maximum of **eight members**, half of whom are to be judicial members, and at least 50% of the members are to be from SC/ST/OBCs, minorities, or women.
 
• The jurisdiction of the Lokpal includes central government employees, public servants, and institutions receiving significant funding from the central government.
 
• It has the power to order a **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** inquiry, prosecute public servants, and ensure fair trials in corruption cases.
 
• The Lokpal is autonomous and functions without interference from the executive or legislature. This independence is crucial to ensuring transparency and accountability.
 
• **The Finance Commission**, **Election Commission**, and **Union Public Service Commission** are constitutional bodies, but they do not investigate corruption complaints. *Hence, the correct option is Lokpal.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:**

 
 
• **The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act** was passed in **December 2013** and came into effect on **16th January 2014**. It was enacted to combat corruption in public administration and ensure accountability.
 
• The Act mandates the appointment of Lokpal at the central level and Lokayuktas in the states, although the structure and jurisdiction of Lokayuktas are determined by the respective state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Structure and Powers of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal is headed by a **Chairperson**, who is or has been the Chief Justice of India, a Supreme Court Judge, or an eminent person with expertise in anti-corruption policies.
 
• It has the power to investigate complaints of corruption against public functionaries, including the Prime Minister (with certain exceptions related to national security and foreign affairs).
 
• The Lokpal has its own investigation and prosecution wings to carry out inquiries and ensure legal proceedings against corrupt officials.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal is empowered to confiscate and attach assets acquired through corrupt means, even during the investigation process.
 
• The selection process for Lokpal members is conducted by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Leader of the Opposition, Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge, and an eminent jurist.
 
• The Lokpal is required to present an annual report to the President of India, which is tabled in Parliament for discussion and accountability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Bodies:**

 
 
• **Finance Commission:** It is a constitutional body under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution. It recommends the distribution of financial resources between the central and state governments but does not handle corruption cases.
 
• **Election Commission:** A constitutional body under **Article 324**, it conducts free and fair elections in India but is not empowered to investigate corruption complaints.
 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC):** Established under **Article 315**, it conducts recruitment exams for civil services and other posts. It does not deal with corruption-related issues.
 
 
 
• **Noteworthy Examples:**
 
 
• **2019:** The first Chairperson of Lokpal, **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**, was appointed along with eight other members.
 
• The Lokpal has been instrumental in addressing corruption cases, ensuring transparency and accountability in public administration.
